claims.text: Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 forms several primary non-eutectic crystalline phases during slower cooling.
Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 exhibits a multistep crystallization sequence upon reheating.
Increasing the melt-spinning quench rate beyond the current rapid-cooling boundary will suppress early formation of primary non-eutectic phases.
Increasing wheel speed is a means of increasing the melt-spinning cooling rate.
The proposed cooling rate must exceed the baseline rapid-cooling rate used in prior processing.
A higher cooling rate reduces the time available for atomic diffusion and nucleation.
Reduced time for diffusion and nucleation minimizes formation of primary non-eutectic crystalline phases.
Further acceleration of cooling suppresses atomic mobility sufficiently to bypass nucleation and growth of early crystalline phases.
Bypassing early crystallization produces a higher retained amorphous-phase fraction.
A higher retained amorphous-phase fraction improves thermal stability during reheating.
Enhanced quenching will yield a higher amorphous-phase fraction than baseline rapid cooling.
Enhanced quenching will shift the onset of exothermic crystallization to higher temperatures during reheating.
Baseline rapid and slower cooling regimes produce multiple primary crystalline phases.
Baseline processing is associated with a complex, multistep crystallization sequence upon reheating.
The baseline and enhanced-quench samples will be compared under identical DSC reheating conditions.
X-ray diffraction will be used to quantify amorphous and crystalline phase fractions.
DSC will be used to measure crystallization onset temperatures and exothermic peaks.
